draft.title: Converting units of area
card: Area units are squared, so the length conversion is squared too. Since \(1 \text{ cm} = 10 \text{ mm}\), a square \(1 \text{ cm}\) by \(1 \text{ cm}\) is \(10 \text{ mm}\) by \(10 \text{ mm}\). So \(1 \text{ cm}^{2} = 100 \text{ mm}^{2}\).

In the same way, \(1 \text{ m} = 100 \text{ cm}\) gives \(1 \text{ m}^{2} = 10{,}000 \text{ cm}^{2}\). Also, \(1 \text{ km} = 1000 \text{ m}\) gives \(1 \text{ km}^{2} = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ m}^{2}\). A hectare (ha) is a unit for land, and \(1 \text{ ha} = 10{,}000 \text{ m}^{2}\).
To go to a smaller unit, multiply. To go to a larger unit, divide. Example: \(3 \text{ m}^{2} = 3 \times 10{,}000 = 30{,}000 \text{ cm}^{2}\).

Choose a unit that suits the size. Use \(\text{mm}^{2}\) or \(\text{cm}^{2}\) for small things such as a stamp, \(\text{m}^{2}\) for a room, ha for a farm or a park, and \(\text{km}^{2}\) for a large region.
draft.remember: Square the length conversion: \(1 \text{ cm}^{2} = 100 \text{ mm}^{2}\), and \(1 \text{ m}^{2} = 10{,}000 \text{ cm}^{2}\).

a.q: Which is the same as \(5 \text{ cm}^{2}\)?
a.why: Going from \(\text{cm}^{2}\) to the smaller \(\text{mm}^{2}\), multiply by 100: \(5 \times 100 = 500\). Multiplying by 10 gives 50, which is the length conversion and forgets that area is squared.

b.q: Priya's farm in Dubbo has an area of \(80{,}000 \text{ m}^{2}\). What is this in hectares?
b.why: One hectare is \(10{,}000 \text{ m}^{2}\), so divide: \(80{,}000 \div 10{,}000 = 8\). Going to a larger unit means dividing, so multiplying would give a much bigger number, which is wrong.
b.clue: You are changing to a larger unit, so divide.
